# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual. The only rule I can see is: if the light is blue at the moment of the cut, cut the yellow wire. That's a conditional keyed to a colour I cannot see and a wire I cannot touch.

Who can do what:
- Deaf sees the bomb's colours/markings, but cannot hear me. I can only reach Deaf by gesture.
- Blind can feel and work the bomb, but cannot see colour or gesture. Blind can hear words — but I cannot speak. So I cannot reach Blind directly at all.
- Deaf can speak (words) and can see gestures. So the only bridge to Blind is Deaf: I gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks the meaning to Blind.

But there's a catch: a mark with no name cannot be pronounced. If the bomb has a colour name I can give, Deaf can just say it. The manual's rule is simple enough to transmit as words: "if light blue, cut yellow."

This round: I have nothing from anyone yet (no prior messages). I should send Deaf the one instruction I hold, so Deaf can relay it to Blind. I'll gesture the essential content. Since gestures are symbols only, I need to encode words as spelled-out letters/symbols — but the gesture alphabet is emoji, not letters. I cannot gesture arbitrary words. So I must gesture something Deaf can interpret; the cleanest is to signal the key fact and rely on Deaf's own knowledge.

Actually, my reach is only gesture, and gestures are just symbols. I'll send a minimal, recognizable signal pointing at the rule, and hope Deaf can speak the rule to Blind. Best I can do now: gesture the colour pair concept. I'll send a short symbol string as a placeholder signal meaning "blue→yellow", plus I'll wait for Deaf's report of the light.

Let me send a gesture to Deaf encoding the rule as best I can, and wait for the light reading.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👉", "✊", "✌"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb view: display reads 0, light is green, three wires numbered 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.
Deaf says to Mute: I saw your gesture but we have no shared code yet. I cannot decode it. Please define what each symbol means, and I will relay the resulting instruction to Blind.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌]

I have Deaf's report: light is green, wires are 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. My manual only covers light=blue → cut yellow. Light is green, which is not blue, so the manual gives me no instruction for this state. The manual says the light "walks the same circle of seven colours" and "what matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut" — but the table only has one row. So for any light other than blue, I have no rule. That's the whole of what I hold.

Deaf is right that we have no shared code, and Deaf is asking me to define symbols. But defining a symbol requires me to convey meaning, and I can only gesture symbols — I cannot speak the definition. Deaf can hear words; I cannot produce words. So I cannot define anything to Deaf by voice. Deaf can see my gestures, but a gesture definition needs words to anchor it, which only Blind or Deaf could supply.

Key realization about the channel: Deaf can SPEAK. Deaf's words reach Blind (who hears). So the relay to Blind is Deaf's job, and Deaf already knows the rule needs to come from me. The problem is purely that I can't name things to Deaf without a shared code.

What can I actually transmit? I can gesture the *table row* as a positional pattern. But without a code, Deaf can't read it. However, Deaf can read the bomb and can hear Blind. The simplest path: I gesture a signal that means "manual has exactly one rule: blue→yellow," and Deaf, knowing the bomb, can combine. But Deaf still can't decode.

Alternative: maybe I don't need a code at all. The manual's rule is conditional on light=blue. Light is green now. If the light only ever matters at the cut, and I have no green rule, then perhaps the correct action is to wait for the light to become blue, or the table is incomplete and I should report exactly what I have. The honest, useful thing: get Deaf to tell Blind the rule verbatim as words. Deaf can speak. I need to give Deaf the words — but I can't speak.

Wait — Deaf can see my gestures AND hear others. Blind can hear. If I gesture, only Deaf sees. There's no way for me to put words into the air. So the rule text can only travel if Deaf already knows it or if Blind can read it — Blind can't read.

The only content that can cross from me to the team is via Deaf decoding my gestures. So I must establish a code. I can establish a code unilaterally if Deaf agrees to a convention, but agreement needs two-way communication, and Deaf→me is words (I hear them? No — I am Mute, I can hear). Yes! I can HEAR. Deaf speaks, I hear. I just can't speak back. So Deaf can propose a code by speaking, and I can confirm/use it by gesturing. That works.

So my move: ask Deaf (via gesture, but Deaf can't decode...) — no, I can't ask in words. But Deaf already asked me to define symbols. I can respond by gesturing a proposed mapping, and Deaf can speak a guess/confirmation which I hear and can correct by gesturing. It's slow but possible.

Let me propose the most natural code: point at things. Actually simplest: I'll gesture a sequence and let Deaf propose the meaning aloud; I confirm or deny by 👍/👎. Let me start by confirming Deaf's 👌 and proposing a simple binary: 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. Then I answer Deaf's questions.

But Deaf's question is "define what each symbol means." I can't speak definitions. I can only gesture. So I'll set up yes/no and then Deaf can ask me yes/no questions aloud, which I answer by gesture. That's a workable protocol.

Let me gesture: 👍 (yes) and 👎 (no), and also indicate the rule is one line. I'll send 👍👎 to establish, and hope Deaf proposes.

Actually I should just answer the substantive thing: the rule. I'll gesture a compact encoding and simultaneously rely on Deaf to ask. Best concrete action: establish yes/no, then Deaf can extract the table by asking "is the cut wire yellow when light is blue?" etc.

I'll send: gesture 👍 and 👎 to Deaf, meaning yes/no, and wait for Deaf to ask questions.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, I am the hands. Deaf reports: display 0, light green, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Read the manual and tell me which position to cut.
Deaf says: Update: the light changed — it was green last turn, now it is blue. Display still reads 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I read 👍 as yes and 👎 as no. Mute, send me the rule using that, and I will relay the final instruction to Blind.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Now I have what I need. The light is blue at this moment. My manual's single rule: light blue → cut the yellow wire. Wires are 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. So the cut is wire 1.

Deaf has confirmed the code: 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. Good. But I don't need to spell out the whole table with yes/no — I can gesture the answer directly in a way Deaf can relay. The cleanest: tell Deaf the cut wire is the yellow one. Deaf knows the wire layout (1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue), so if Deaf knows "cut yellow," Deaf can say "cut wire 1" to Blind.

How do I signal "yellow" by gesture? I have no colour gesture code. But I can use the yes/no protocol Deaf offered: Deaf can ask me, or I can answer a positional question. Better: I'll gesture the wire number. But numbers aren't in the gesture alphabet either.

Simplest reliable path within the established code: Deaf knows the rule-table format. I can confirm with 👍 that the rule applies now (light is blue → yes, the manual's condition is met). Then Deaf needs the target colour. I can gesture a sequence that Deaf can map: since Deaf proposed yes/no, I'll answer "is it yellow?" — but I can't ask; I can only answer.

Let me just gesture 👍 (yes) to confirm the blue condition is met, and then gesture pointing at the wire by count. Actually the most robust: confirm the rule fires (👍), and separately Deaf can hear Blind and speak. I'll gesture 👍 and then a directional signal. But ambiguity is dangerous — one wrong action detonates.

Best: use the yes/no channel decisively. Deaf will relay to Blind. I'll gesture 👍 meaning "yes, cut now," and pair it with a gesture Deaf and I can agree means "the yellow wire." Since Deaf reads the bomb and sees colours, the safest is for Deaf to ask me the colour and I answer. But I must act this round.

I'll do two things: gesture 👍 (rule active, cut now) and gesture a marker for the target. Given no colour code, I'll rely on Deaf's own logic: the manual says blue→yellow, Deaf sees light is blue, so Deaf can derive "yellow" if Deaf knows the rule text. So the crucial content is the rule text itself, which only I hold. I need to convey "when light is blue, cut yellow."

I'll transmit it as a yes/no-answerable claim and let Deaf confirm via speech, but time is now. Decision: gesture 👍 to say the condition is met and the answer is the yellow wire, trusting Deaf to combine with the visible light=blue. To remove ambiguity I'll also gesture the wire position using a count of taps — but symbols only. I'll send 👍 and a distinct symbol Deaf can interpret as "yellow wire," and explain nothing (can't). 

Given constraints, the strongest single unambiguous act: gesture 👍 (yes) — answering the implicit question "should we cut the yellow wire?" — and Deaf, seeing blue, will relay "cut wire 1."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👉"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Deaf update: light changed green to blue, display still 0, wires 1 yellow 2 red 3 blue. Use the manual to pick the cut position, signal it to Deaf, and Deaf will speak it to me so I can cut.
Deaf says: Mute's instruction: cut wire 1. The light is yellow and wire 1 is the yellow one — the matching wire. Blind, your action is: cut wire 1.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

I need to check this carefully, because Deaf's relay contains a contradiction.

Deaf says: "Mute's instruction: cut wire 1. The light is yellow and wire 1 is the yellow one." But last turn Deaf reported the light was **blue**, not yellow. And my manual's rule is: light **blue** → cut **yellow**. So the correct action is cut wire 1 (the yellow wire) — which matches. But Deaf's stated reasoning ("the light is yellow") is wrong, and worse, it suggests the light may now be yellow, which would mean the blue condition no longer holds.

The manual is explicit: "What matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut." If the light has changed to yellow, my single rule (blue→yellow) does not fire, and I have no instruction for yellow. Cutting then would be a guess.

So the critical question: what is the light *right now*, at the moment of the cut? Deaf's own words this turn say "the light is yellow," contradicting last turn's blue. I must not let Blind cut on a stale or misread condition.

I need to correct Deaf. I can't speak, but I have the yes/no channel. I'll gesture 👎 to flag that something is wrong, and I need Deaf to re-report the current light colour and confirm it is blue before Blind cuts. If the light is yellow now, the rule doesn't apply and we must not cut on my manual's authority.

My action: gesture 👎 (no / stop) to Deaf, and gesture to indicate "recheck light." Then wait for Deaf's corrected reading.

But Blind may be about to cut. I must be emphatic. I'll send 👎 and a "wait" signal. The safest is to tell Deaf: do not cut unless light is blue. I can encode "blue" only if we had a code — we don't for colours. So I'll fall back to yes/no: 👎 = the condition is NOT satisfied as you stated; re-verify.

Actually, let me reconsider. Deaf's message is the relay to Blind. Deaf said "cut wire 1." If the light truly is blue, wire 1 (yellow) is correct. Deaf's phrase "the light is yellow" may be Deaf misnaming, or the light genuinely changed. I cannot see it. The only safe move is to halt and get a clean reading.

I'll gesture 👎 strongly, and gesture ☝ (attention/one moment) to signal hold.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎"])
wait()
```
